  comment = "#>",

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(scTreeSim)
library(ggtree)
library(dplyr)
source("helpers.R")  # plotting helpers of the vignettes: plot_tree() and a colour-blind safe palette
```

This vignette covers the ways to simulate a tree (by origin time or by number of taxa) under the age-dependent branching process.
Sampling and pruning effects are shown, single- and multi-type trees are presented.
The gene expression and a binary trait on top of a single fixed tree is simulated. 
Barcodes have their own vignette, `vignette("simulate_barcodes")`.

All trees are `treedata` objects (from `treeio`) and are drawn with `ggtree`, with time before present on the axis: 
the dashed lines mark the **origin** of the process and the **present**.

# Simulating trees

Trees are generated by an age-dependent branching process: the lifetime of a cell is
gamma-distributed (`shape`, `scale`; its mean is `shape * scale`, or give `mean_lifetime`),
and at the end of its life a cell dies (with probability `death_prob`) or divides in two.

```{r}
shape <- 100
av_lifetime <- 1
d <- 0.1
scale <- av_lifetime / shape
```

## By origin time

Simulates forward from a single ancestor for a fixed amount of time (`origin_time`), 
so the number of resulting tips is random. The tree contains the lineages that died
along the way (grey tips); the tips alive at the present are green.

```{r}
t_or <- 6
set.seed(5)
tree_by_time <- sim_adb_origin_complete_fast(t_or, scale, shape, d)
plot_tree(tree_by_time, color = "status")
```

## By number of taxa

Simulates forward until a fixed number of living taxa (`ntaxa`) is reached,
so the time span of the tree is random instead (compare the origin on the axis).

```{r}
ntaxa <- 2^5
set.seed(5)
tree_by_ntaxa <- sim_adb_ntaxa_complete_fast(ntaxa, scale, shape, d)
plot_tree(tree_by_ntaxa, color = "status")
```

## Sampling and pruning

`sim_adb_origin_samp()` (and its `ntaxa` counterpart `sim_adb_ntaxa_samp()`) additionally samples
tips at present with probability `sampling_prob` and prunes extinct and unsampled
lineages, giving the tree that is actually observed.

```{r}
set.seed(5)
tree_sampled <- sim_adb_origin_samp(t_or, scale, shape, d, sampling_prob = 0.2)
plot_tree(tree_sampled, color = "status")
```

By default (`collapse = TRUE`) the divisions that lost one of their two lineages are removed, so every
internal node has two children. With `collapse = FALSE` these nodes are kept as
single-child nodes: the same tree has more nodes, but no information on the types and divisions
is lost, as required for the multi-type models and the division-triggered spikes of the binary trait model below.
With the same seed, the simulated tree and the sampled tips are identical in both cases:

```{r}
set.seed(5)
tree_kept <- sim_adb_origin_samp(t_or, scale, shape, d, sampling_prob = 0.2, collapse = FALSE)
c(collapsed = nrow(tree_sampled@data), kept = nrow(tree_kept@data))

plot_tree(tree_kept, color = "status", show_nodes = T)
```

# Multi-type trees

Passing per-type parameters and type-transition matrices (`asym_trans_prob`, `sym_trans_prob`)
simulates a tree in which cells switch between discrete types: at a division, an
asymmetric transition makes one daughter change type, a symmetric one lets both
daughters take the type of their parent. The tree starts in `origin_type`, and the root edge is
colored accordingly. This tree is used for the data below and in `vignette("simulate_barcodes")`.

```{r}
ntype <- 2
origin_type <- 0
shape <- c(100, 1)
av_lifetime <- rep(1, ntype)
scale <- av_lifetime / shape
rho <- 0.8
t_or <- 7
d <- c(0.1, 0.1)

r <- 0.11
Xi_as <- matrix(c(0.0, 0.0, r, 0.0), nrow = ntype, ncol = ntype)
Xi_s  <- matrix(c(1 - r, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0), nrow = ntype, ncol = ntype)

# collapse = FALSE keeps every division node in the tree, including ones
# with only one surviving child -- required for the division-triggered
# spikes used in the binary trait model below
set.seed(2)
mt_tree <- sim_adb_origin_samp(t_or, scale, shape, d, rho, origin_type,
                               asym_trans_prob = Xi_as, sym_trans_prob = Xi_s, collapse = FALSE)
# a simulation with too few tips returns NULL: try another seed
stopifnot(!is.null(mt_tree))
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plot_tree(mt_tree, color = "type", show_nodes = T)
```

# Gene expression (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck)

Simulates one continuous trait per node under an OU process with a
type-dependent optimum (`theta`). `alpha = 0` reduces this to Brownian
motion.

```{r}
# `type` of theta has the same class as `type` in the tree (integer)
theta <- data.frame(type = c(0L, 1L), theta = c(0, 3))
stopifnot(all(unique(mt_tree@data$type) %in% theta$type))

expr <- sim_expression_ou(mt_tree, alpha = 0.5, sigmasq = 0.2, root_value = 0, theta = theta)
head(expr)
```

```{r}
expr %>%
  left_join(mt_tree@data %>% select(node, status), by = "node") %>%
  filter(status == 1) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = factor(type), y = expr, fill = factor(type))) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = type_cols) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "type", y = "expression at the tips")
```

# Gene expression for multiple genes

`sim_expression_matrix()` runs the OU model for several genes on the same tree.
`alpha`, `sigmasq` and `root_value` take one value per gene (or a single value shared by
all genes), and `theta` is a data frame with the `type` column and one column of optima
per gene. The number of genes is given by the length of these parameters, and `gene_names`
optionally names the genes (default: 1, ..., N).

```{r}
theta_genes <- data.frame(type = c(0L, 1L),
                          g1 = c(0, 3),   # higher in type 1
                          g2 = c(1, 1),   # same in both types
                          g3 = c(2, 0))   # lower in type 1

expr_mat <- sim_expression_matrix(mt_tree, alpha = c(0.5, 0.5, 1), sigmasq = 0.2,
                                  root_value = 0, theta = theta_genes,
                                  gene_names = c("gene1", "gene2", "gene3"))
head(expr_mat)
```

## Many genes, with parameters drawn from priors

To simulate hundreds of genes, `sim_gene_params()` draws the parameters of every gene from priors
(`sim_prior()`): each gene is a Brownian motion (`alpha = 0`) or an OU process, whose optima in the types
are separated by `eta`. It returns the table of true parameters, one row per gene, and does not set the seed:
call `set.seed()` first to get the same genes again. `gene_optima()` arranges the optima as the `theta` of
`sim_expression_matrix()`. To specify the parameters yourself, `gene_params_from_table()` builds the same table
from a data frame with the columns `alpha`, `sigma2` and `theta_0`, `theta_1`, ...

```{r}
set.seed(4)
genes <- sim_gene_params(mt_tree, n_genes = 6, n_types = 2, pi_ou = 0.5,
                         alpha = sim_prior("exponential", rate = 1, lower = 0.1),
                         eta = sim_prior("exponential", rate = 1))
genes[c("gene", "class_eff", "alpha", "sigma2", "theta_0", "theta_1")]

expr_genes <- sim_expression_matrix(mt_tree, alpha = genes$alpha, sigmasq = genes$sigma2,
                                    root_value = genes$x_root, theta = gene_optima(genes),
                                    gene_names = genes$gene)
```

`summarize_expression()` reports quick sanity checks of the genes (and `summarize_tree()`, `summarize_snv()`,
`summarize_binary()`, `summarize_barcodes()` and `summarize_counts()` those of the other layers; they return the
numbers, and `print()` shows them as text). `plot_sim_umap()` embeds the cells from their latent expression with UMAP
and colours them by cell type; it needs the package `uwot`, and takes a `seed`, as UMAP uses random numbers.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("uwot", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
summarize_expression(expr_genes, mt_tree, genes)
plot_sim_umap(expr_genes, mt_tree, seed = 1)
```

# Single-cell gene expression counts

`sim_expression_counts_matrix()` turns the expression values at the tips into counts, one
negative binomial draw per gene and cell, with mean `size_factor * exp(expr)` and dispersion
`phi` (one value per gene, or a single shared value). The tree is needed to identify the
sampled tips, which are the cells. Optionally, `size_factor` gives a per-cell scaling
(e.g. library size), named by the node ids of the tips and shared by all genes.

```{r}
set.seed(3)
counts <- sim_expression_counts_matrix(expr_mat, mt_tree, phi = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5))
head(counts)
```

```{r}
# the same cells with different library sizes
tips <- mt_tree@data$node[mt_tree@data$status == 1]
size_factor <- setNames(rlnorm(length(tips), meanlog = 0, sdlog = 0.3), as.character(tips))
counts_sf <- sim_expression_counts_matrix(expr_mat, mt_tree, phi = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5),
                                          size_factor = size_factor)
```

`sim_count_params()` draws the dispersion of every gene (from a prior, or following a trend with the level
of the gene) and the size factor of every cell, and can shift the expression so that the mean count has a
given value:

```{r}
set.seed(5)
count_params <- sim_count_params(expr_genes, mt_tree, genes, cell_size_sd = 0.5, target_mean_count = 2)
counts_genes <- sim_expression_counts_matrix(count_params$expr, mt_tree, phi = count_params$phi,
                                             size_factor = count_params$size_factor)
```

```{r}
counts %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = factor(type), y = gene1, fill = factor(type))) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = type_cols) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "type", y = "counts of gene1")
```

# Binary trait, with error and division-triggered spikes

A binary trait evolving under a 2-state CTMC along the tree, with a strict
clock, division-triggered spikes and false positive/negative error at the tips.
Each daughter branch of a division gets a gamma-distributed spike (mean 0.05 expected
substitutions per site), three times larger when a type-1 cell divides.

```{r}
clk <- clock_strict(0.5, spike = spike(0.05, shape = 2, by_type = c(1, 3)))
bc_binary <- sim_binary(mt_tree, n_sites = 10, clock = clk, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.02)
head(bc_binary)
```

See `vignette("simulate_binary")` for the substitution model, the clock models and spikes.
Diploid SNVs under the GT16 model use the same clock models, see `vignette("simulate_SNV")`.
